sections.name: SlugRedirect
sections.title: Redirect on load
sections.what: After the page loads, replaces the address with the application screen address that includes the slug. Shows REDIRECTING while it runs.
sections.why: Replacing instead of adding a new history entry stops the back button from returning to this step.
sections.watch_out: The slug is inserted into the address without encoding.

summary: A browser step that moves the visitor from the slug address to the real application screen, showing REDIRECTING while it works.
purpose: Sends visitors to the single application screen, which reads the slug from the address.
why: Likely reason: one screen that reads the slug from the query string works for any slug, including ones not built ahead of time. The code does not state this.
how: After the page loads, replaces the current address with the application screen address that includes the slug. Shows a short REDIRECTING message while this happens.
inputs: The slug string from the parent page, and the router.
outputs: A browser navigation and a short message on screen.
risks: The slug is placed into the address without encoding, so unusual characters could break the link. Replacing the history means the back button skips this page.
debug: If the page stays on REDIRECTING, check that the slug is valid and that the target page loads. Open the target address directly to see whether the redirect or the target is the problem.
